Evelyn's eyes narrowed as she sat in her small apartment, surrounded by stacks of books. She had always been a huge fan of author Rachel Kim, whose lyrical prose and vivid characters had transported Evelyn to far-off worlds. But now, her trust was shattered. A review article on her phone proclaimed that several of Rachel's most popular novels contained stolen passages from lesser-known authors.

Evelyn's fingers were clenched into fists as she scrolled through the online forum where the allegations were being debated. She couldn't believe it – how could someone she admired so much betray her like this? The words "thief" and "fraudster" flashed in her mind, but she pushed them aside along with other vicious thoughts.

Her gaze dropped to Rachel's latest novel, still unopened on her nightstand. How dare the woman even release a new book now, after everything that had come to light? Evelyn ripped off her headphones and hurled them across the room, as if the sound was too much for her to bear. In the sudden silence, she let out a low growl.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
story:
Alex's jawline flexed as he slammed his laptop shut on the living room couch. The news reports were flooding in – Rachel Kim had been caught plagiarizing. For years, Alex had read every book of hers, devouring the way she wove words into magic. Now it seemed she'd been doing more than weaving: she'd stolen from others and presented it as her own.

Alex's face flushed with heat, his heart thudding in protest against this betrayal. He thought about all the times he'd spent discussing Rachel's work with friends, singing its praises on social media...Had they ever praised a plagiarist? The very thought made him twitchy.

With no interest left in sitting around the computer, Alex stood up and began to pace between the living room furniture. His mind kept straying to the authors from whom Rachel had allegedly stolen – how must their feelings have been when they realized their work was being passed off as someone else's? As he stomped back into his bedroom, a fierce cry still locked in his chest.

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
story:
Ava hunched over her desk, nursing a cold cup of coffee. Every so often, she looked up at the shelf above her computer, where about five volumes of Rachel Kim's novels proudly resided. Those shelves now stood empty but for one book – her favorite among Rachel's works, still closed on top. How could Ava have been blind to her idol's deceit? The realization felt like a kick in the gut.

Her legs were folded tightly under her as she leaned forward, fingers clutching the wooden edge of the table. She replayed conversations with friends and family over dinner, mentioning Rachel's latest releases as if all love stories came wrapped up with an "R" label, implying that only authors named Rachel could craft them so well.

Her grip on the coffee began to slacken; it dropped to her toes without spilling thanks to some miracle. Her mind whirred faster than a fan in an overheated room – who was behind these plagiarism allegations? And what did Rachel know now about her own reputation?

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
story:
Jesse stood alone by the large, high desk at his workspace, arms stiff and still as he clutched his mouse in one hand. Fanning out on the bright work surface were all the screen shots of the plagiarized scenes: text-heavy and colorless, like a crime scene investigation waiting to be solved.

Jesse remembered attending Rachel Kim's reading just two months back and how she'd seemed genuinely warm with her audience, as if her words only grew bolder because they carried within them an element of truth – not the truth that it originated from other minds but the very notion of a world that was hers alone to shape. And here Jesse was today, his gaze fixed on her words: the lies. How the hell did he trust someone anymore?

topic: Someone learns their favorite author plagiarized their stories
story:
Leigh sat cross-legged at the edge of her bed with an unopened box of tissues lying abandoned beside her. Her eyes remained on Rachel Kim's book that lay open across her lap – or rather, not so open; Leigh simply stopped at a certain line where she'd learned it would reek of Rachel's shame.

That morning, Leigh had spent some quality time scrolling through Twitter, absorbing the latest development without taking in much of the words surrounding them. Her phone buzzed to notify another opinion, article analysis on a web site that was normally quite reliable; it stung – and it wasn't even a harsh thing that she'd read somewhere else already.

Still running a dry tongue along her lips, Leigh realized with some surprise how long ago her crush began, what memories lingered of when they thought it was art being crafted not only by Rachel's fingers but by some greater spirit which allowed for inspiration. Fidgety now and distracted with little movements, Leigh picked up the book slowly as she tried to put together those very different threads in Rachel's tangled legacy that were so disheartening.

The scene cut black just when Leigh raised her hand; before it settled back onto the bed sheet.
